honesty: Cost is simulated: the graph features are precomputed in this dataset, so cost is modelled as local = 1 and graph = r times local.
The share of transactions escalated on test (6.8%) is much lower than on validation (19.5%) because the illicit share fell between the periods. It is reported, not corrected.
Evaluation is on the test steps 35-49, scored once with thresholds frozen on earlier steps.
Transaction ids are the dataset's own anonymised ids; no real-world identity is shown or implied.
After step 42 every system collapses to near-zero F1 (temporal drift); the cascade does not fix that.
Recall retention is a weak test on this split: local-only recall is already close to graph-always recall.
The Stage 2 threshold d2 was chosen on 19.6%-illicit calibration steps and did not transfer well to the 6.5%-illicit test steps.
One chronological split and one model family; results are not a guarantee on future data.
The cascade F1 (0.798) is above graph-always (0.762) largely because graph-always, at its frozen threshold, raises many false alarms; this is not evidence that the cascade is a better model.
